reading.title: Чтение
reading.about: 3 текста разной сложности, по 4 вопроса к каждому. Текст можно перечитывать сколько угодно.

parts.title: Текст 1 · Сообщение команде
parts.passage:
Hi all,

A quick update about the design review on Thursday. We're moving it from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., because the product manager has a call with a client in the morning.

The review will be in Room 4, not online, so please come to the office if you can. If you can't, add your comments to the shared document by Wednesday evening.

Please bring printed copies of your two best screens — we'll put them on the wall and vote for the strongest ideas.

Thanks,
Daniel

items.q: What time is the review now?
Why has the time changed?
options: Room 4 is busy in the morning
The product manager has a call with a client
Daniel is away on Thursday morning

items.q: What should people who can't come do?
options: Add comments to the shared document by Wednesday evening
Send their printed screens to Daniel

items.q: What will happen to the printed screens?
options: They'll go on the wall, and people will vote
The product manager will choose the best one
They'll be sent to the client

parts.title: Текст 2 · Статья о дизайн-ревью
parts.passage:
For years, the design team at a mid-sized travel company presented finished work to managers once a month. The meetings were long, and feedback often arrived too late: by the time someone pointed out a problem, developers had already started building.

Last spring, the team tried something different. Instead of monthly presentations, they began sharing rough sketches in short weekly sessions with developers and support staff. Nobody was allowed to say whether they liked a design; people could only ask questions or describe what a user might struggle with.

At first, some designers felt uncomfortable showing unfinished work. "It felt like going out before you're properly dressed," one of them admitted. But after a couple of months, the number of late changes had fallen by almost half, and support staff were spotting problems that designers had missed, because they spoke to customers every day.

The team's lead says the biggest benefit was not speed. "People stopped defending their designs and started discussing the problem," she explains.

items.q: What was the main problem with the monthly presentations?
options: Feedback came after development had started

items.q: In the weekly sessions, people were not allowed to…
options: say whether they liked a design
describe what users might struggle with

items.q: Why were support staff especially useful?
options: They talked to customers every day

items.q: According to the team lead, the most important change was that…
options: people focused on the problem instead of defending their work

parts.title: Текст 3 · Статья о метриках
parts.passage:
Few things are as tempting to a manager as a number that goes up. Tickets closed, screens delivered, hours logged — each promises a clear picture of who is working hard. Yet economists have long warned about what is known as Goodhart's law: once a measure becomes a target, it stops being a good measure.

The problem is not that people cheat, although some do. It is that any single number captures only part of the job, and people naturally shift their effort towards the part that is counted. A designer judged on the number of screens delivered has little reason to spend a day talking to users, even if that conversation would save weeks of rework.

This does not mean that measurement is useless. Teams that use several indicators together, and treat them as starting points for conversation rather than verdicts, tend to avoid the worst distortions. What matters, researchers suggest, is less what is measured than how the results are used.

Some critics go further, arguing that the most valuable work — mentoring a colleague, noticing a problem before it appears — is precisely the kind that resists measurement. Their point is not to abandon numbers, but to remember what they leave out.

items.q: What does Goodhart's law say, as described in the text?
options: A measure loses its value when it becomes a target

items.q: According to the text, why does a single number cause problems?
options: It is difficult to calculate correctly
Most people cheat to improve it
People focus their effort on what is counted

items.q: The writer suggests that measurement works better when…
options: results start a discussion rather than act as a final judgement
a team uses only one clear indicator
results are not shared with the team

items.q: What is the critics' main point?
options: Some of the most valuable work is hard to measure
Mentoring matters more than design work

lines.t: Hi, I've started on the settings screen. Quick question about the toggle states.
In the file there's an 'on' and an 'off' state, but nothing for when the setting is loading. What should people see while we wait for the server?
Good catch — I didn't design that. For now, let's show the toggle in grey and disable it. I'll add a proper loading state to the file by tomorrow morning.
Great. And on smaller phones, some labels wrap onto two lines. Is that okay?
Two lines is fine, but not three. If a label needs three lines, let me know and I'll shorten the text.

items.q: What is the developer working on?
What was missing from the design file?
What will people see while the setting is loading, for now?
options: A grey toggle that doesn't work

items.q: What does the designer say about long labels?
options: Three lines is fine on small phones
Labels must fit on one line

lines.t: Thanks for coming. I'd like to share one lesson from our user interviews this quarter.

We spoke to twenty small business owners about how they send invoices. Almost all of them said the process was easy. However, when we asked them to show us how they actually did it, most of them used two or three different tools and copied numbers by hand.
In other words, what people say and what people do are often quite different — not because they're lying, but because they've got used to the extra steps and no longer notice them.

So my suggestion for next quarter is simple: in every interview, let's spend at least half the time watching people complete a real task, rather than asking them to describe it. We'll get fewer quotes for our slides, but far more useful findings.

items.q: What did most business owners say about sending invoices?
What did the researchers notice when they watched?
options: People used several tools and copied numbers by hand
People made many mistakes in the numbers
People refused to show their process

items.q: According to the speaker, why do people describe the process inaccurately?
options: They want to impress the researchers
They no longer notice the extra steps

items.q: What trade-off does the speaker accept?
options: Fewer quotes for presentations, but more useful findings
Less time watching, but more participants

speaking.title: Говорение
speaking.about: Говорение проходит голосом в чате **Speaking**: напишите там «контрольная». ≈ 12–15 минут, 3 части, как в Cambridge и IELTS Speaking: вопросы о себе, рассказ по карточке, обсуждение. Ошибки по ходу не исправляются. В конце Claude даст отчёт — перенесите его в чат «Экспорт / импорт», и результат придёт сюда сам.
